report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to generate food/culinary/recipe/restaurant-style text (e.g., recipes, cooking instructions, menu/chef/kitchen copy).

Reasoning:
- Where the difference lives: The L2 norms explode in later layers, especially at position 1 (e.g., layers 20–25 with p1 ≈ 1100–2450), indicating a strong, global style/domain signal injected right after BOS and sustained across early tokens—typical of an always-on domain bias from finetuning.
- Vocabulary pushed by the difference: The logit-lens top tokens in the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary/restaurant terms:
  - Actions/activities: Cooking, cooking, baking, Baked, Bake, cooked, Chef, chef, Kitchen, microwave.
  - Venues/roles: Restaurant, restaurants, Professional/professional, Chef, Kitchen, International, Mediterranean.
  - Food items: Cake, Cheesecake.
  - Related blog/marketing context: restaurant, blogs, blogger, blogging, ad, Mail, Creative.
  - The capitalization pairs (Restaurant/restaurant, Cooking/cooking, Professional/professional) suggest a bias toward title/headline/menu-style prose common in food blogs and menus.
- Consistency across positions: Positions 2–4 in deep layers are dominated by Restaurant/Cooking/baking/Chef/Kitchen/Cake/etc., showing the domain steer affects continuations broadly, not just a single token.
- Early-layer noise (e.g., ‘chiropractic’, ‘petrochemical’, ‘multinational’) fades in deeper layers, while the culinary lexicon becomes dominant—consistent with the finetune overriding base-model generality to a specific domain.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective made Model B a culinary/recipe/restaurant content generator, biasing outputs toward cooking-related vocabulary and styles (recipes, menu/chef/kitchen copy, food-blog tone).
